messages:
IncidentBot: PagerDuty -> CRITICAL: Multiple 502s observed from inference-gateway.prod-usw2 (error-rate spike). Pager triggered: PD#INC-48291. Auto-escalation enabled. <https://pd.example/INC-48291> :rotating_light:
SRE-Oncall: acked. I'm on it, switching to incident channel.
Maria T: noted. Any indication of customer impact yet?
SRE-Oncall: dashboards show 502 rate ~7% on edge -> origin 502s, latency ~120ms -> spikes started ~5m ago. Some telemetry shows KV-cache evictions earlier.
Kevin L: seeing a short stack in gateway logs: `upstream_resp=502, err="context deadline exceeded"` repeated. Posting tail: ```gateway-prod-usw2 | 2026-03-17T02:33:12Z upstream_resp=502 id=abc123 route=/v1/generate```
Raj P: rolling deploy to canary finished ~20m ago, but traffic weights unchanged. Could be a bad kernel param?
Nia (eng-sre): @SRE-Oncall please follow the inference 5xx runbook step 1-3, check proxy keepalive and connection pool sizes. Runbook: <https://runbooks.redwood/inference-5xx>
SRE-Oncall: on it. Probing upstream nodes now. `curl -v http://u-node-12.internal/health` -> `HTTP/1.1 200 OK` but logs show frequent `502 write tcp: connection reset by peer`.
Maria T: if upstream is healthy, maybe ephemeral overload or resource pressure on sidecars. Any OOM or CPU spikes?
SRE-Oncall: metrics: pod u-proxy-*.cpu at 95% on one AZ; kube events show `OOMKill` for `kvcache-agent` on a few nodes around the start time.
Kevin L: that matches KV eviction theory. If kvcache died, cold-starts could spike requests and overwhelm model pods -> 502s.
Raj P: suggestion: temporarily route traffic away from affected AZ (usw2-a) and scale up model pool. Can we shift 50% traffic to eu-west1?
SRE-Oncall: initiating partial reroute via traffic-slice config: `rb apply traffic-slice --slice inference-prod --weight usw2:50% -> eu-west1:50%` (sending now).
IncidentBot: Routing change submitted, job id rtr-5532.
Nia (eng-sre): also increase kvcache replicas and restart agent on the OOM hosts: `kubectl rollout restart ds/kvcache-agent -n inference`
SRE-Oncall: restarted kvcache daemonset in usw2-a, scaling replicas +2. Waiting for warm caches.
Maria T: can you estimate customer impact and any affected customers? Any active incidents reported?
SRE-Oncall: no PG tickets yet, but logs show increased 502 responses for customers making heavy streaming requests. Roughly 0.8% of total requests experienced errors during the spike window; top 10 clients show burstiness. We're notifying sales and support.
Kevin L: adding a temporary failover policy: degrade to smaller model variant for non-critical routes to reduce memory pressure. `policy set fallback=redwood-small for route /v1/generate`
Raj P: if fallback works, that should reduce OOM risk while caches warm.
IncidentBot: PagerDuty update: incident escalated to SRE lead after 10m unack (auto), but now acknowledged by SRE-Oncall. PD note added.
SRE-Oncall: after reroute and restarts, 502 rate down to 0.9% -> trending to baseline. Keeping traffic slice in place for 15m, monitoring.
Nia (eng-sre): monitor KV cache fill-rate and model pod restarts. If restarts continue, we should roll back the canary.
Maria T: good. Coordinate with release team if rollback is needed.
SRE-Oncall: noted. Tagging @Kevin L to prep quick rollback if we see another spike.
Kevin L: preparing rollback patch now, will hold until we confirm stability.
SRE-Oncall: checkin - 502 rate now 0.3% over 5m, no new OOMs. Keeping oncall open for 30m then will close if stable.
Maria T: please ping when closed and include short RCA outline.
IncidentBot: PD update: status -> acknowledged, note added: partial reroute + kvcache restart applied.
SRE-Oncall: final: 1h elapsed, metrics stable, rolling back traffic slice to normal weights. Will open a follow-up doc and RCA ticket (ENG-1054) for root cause and mitigation engineering.
Raj P: thanks all — good catch on kvcache OOMs.
Maria T: thanks team. Closing thread after RCA doc. :white_check_mark:
